close_reason: Resolved by inspection 2026-05-11. RevocationChecker::check_revocation(cert, issuer) is per-cert by design; verify_chain at pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:172-181 calls it in a loop. Granularity is per-cert and already in production.
description:
**Options:**

- **A) Per-path single mode.** Caller passes `RevocationMode::HardFail | SoftFail | Disabled`; applies uniformly to every cert in chain. Simpler.
- **B) Per-cert mode.** Caller can request hard-fail EE OCSP but soft-fail intermediate CRL (common operational pattern). More expressive.
- **C) Per-source mode.** OCSP vs CRL different. Most granular; rarely needed in practice.

Operational reality: B is what production deployments actually want. CT log monitors and CAs themselves typically: hard-fail EE OCSP, soft-fail intermediate CRL, disable revocation for root anchors. A forces caller to pick the most lenient mode (which weakens EE checking) or the strictest (which causes intermediate CRL-fetch outages to fail handshakes).

Worth checking: does `pkix-revocation::RevocationChecker` trait already support per-cert mode? If yes, picking B is free.

title: Decide RevocationMode granularity (per-path vs per-cert)
